html:
The Amorúa are a small Indigenous people of the eastern plains of Colombia and Venezuela, near the Orinoco River. They speak a language of the Guahiban family and are close kin of the Sikuani, with whom they are often counted.

Like other peoples of the Orinoco savannas, they lived by moving between rivers and grasslands, fishing, hunting and growing some manioc. Their neighbours included the Achagua. Little was written about them before the 1900s. Today a few hundred live in Vichada in Colombia and in Apure in Venezuela.
